assumptions: The flag toggle at 15:07 was treated as the trigger because it coincides exactly with the onset of the new error type; no change-management record, actor, or intent behind the toggle was retrieved, so it is unknown whether the flip was deliberate, automated, or accidental.

The alternative hypothesis — that the defect was a latent bug already deployed in the non-fallback checkout path and merely became reachable when the flag turned off — was never tested. It is not mutually exclusive with the confirmed cause and is most likely also true; the code itself was not inspected.

Customer-facing impact is inferred from account page request failures in the logs. No user reports, support tickets, or downstream order/payment data were examined, so the real-world consequence for shoppers is assumed rather than observed.

The UpstreamTimeout payment-authorization errors present throughout 15:00-15:06 and again at 15:11 are assumed to be unrelated background noise at the service's normal baseline, not a contributing factor. This was not verified.
Recovery is assumed complete because the service returned to baseline immediately after the flag was restored; no post-mitigation observation window beyond the resolution timestamp was reviewed.
Impact is assumed to be confined to account page rendering. Whether checkout, orders, or other surfaces on the same code path were also affected was not checked.
The gap between the onset of failures at 15:07 and the alert at 15:12:50 is taken from the timestamps; why detection took that long (alert threshold, evaluation window) was not investigated.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, a configuration change to the online shop took effect at 15:07 UTC and caused a significant share of customer account page requests to fail with an error page. The change was a toggle of an internal setting that had been keeping the shop on its older checkout logic; turning it off exposed a defect in the newer logic. Monitoring raised an alert at 15:12:50 UTC, the cause was identified within about a minute, and the setting was restored at 15:14:06 UTC, after which the shop returned to its normal behaviour. Customers affected during the roughly seven minutes of degradation would have seen failed account page loads and could retry successfully afterwards; there is no indication of data loss or of incorrect charges. The underlying defect in the newer checkout logic has not been fixed — the shop is simply back on the older path — so that setting must not be changed again until the defect is found and repaired.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was switched from on to off at 15:07 (partial rollout during that minute, fully off from 15:08), which routed account page requests onto the non-fallback checkout code path; that path raises a ZeroDivisionError, so account page requests began failing immediately and kept failing until the flag was set back on. No deploy occurred in the 11:00-15:07 change window, so the flag flip — not a code push — was the proximate trigger, though the defect itself lives in the code behind the flag.
